ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act, as amended, Articles 1, 289 and 317; Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information, as amended, Articles 2, 5-2, 5-3 and 5-6; Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information, as amended; Real Name Financial Transactions Act, as amended; Local Tax Act, as amended

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Registration Certificate of the Chusik Hoesa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Commercial Registration Office of the Republic of Korea (Seoul Central District Court Commercial Registry if registered in Seoul)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issue the official certificate directly from the court registry; for any foreign filing attach only a Hague Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; do not add consular legalization because the Republic of Korea is a Hague Apostille Convention member state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Subsisting Corporate Status
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Commercial Registration Office of the Republic of Korea for the company, or the national company registry of the ultimate shareholder if issued outside Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a Korean certificate: obtain court-certified copy, attach Hague Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs; for a foreign shareholder certificate issued in a non-Apostille state: obtain notarization, then authentication by the origin state ministry, then legalization by the Consular Division of the Embassy of the Republic of Korea in that origin state; use either Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization exclusively and never chain the two.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney appointing the local incorporator and legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the ultimate corporate shareholder or the governing body of the single-family office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execute before a notary public in the jurisdiction of signing; if the signing jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention state, attach a Hague Apostille from that state competent authority; if the signing jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention state, perform consular legalization through the Korean embassy or consulate in that jurisdiction; the two authentication paths are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the Chusik Hoesa (certified copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public and the District Court Commercial Registration Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the certified copy; attach a Hague Apostille issued by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs; no separate consular legalization is required because Korea is a member of the Hague Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Single-Family-Office relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank holding the intermediate family investment account or the principal private banking relationship of the ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issue on bank letterhead with branch signature and seal; notarize the signatory if required; then attach either a Hague Apostille if the issuing bank jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention state or use Korean consular legalization if the jurisdiction is not a Convention state; never combine apostille and consular legalization for the same letter.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Identification and Ultimate Beneficial Owner Due Diligence File of each natural person UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the UBO nationality, notary public, and the responsible AML compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize certified copies of passports and proof of identity; if needed by the receiving Korean bank, attach a Hague Apostille from the nationality jurisdiction; if the nationality jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention state, use consular legalization at the Korean diplomatic mission; keep the entire UBO file under Government_Only_Access rather than public filing.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to accepting the mandate, counsel and the AML compliance officer must screen every ultimate beneficial owner, all shareholders above the 25 per cent threshold, every director, each officer and any authorised signatory against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Interpol notices, and the watchlists published by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit and the Korea Financial Supervisory Service. The firm must verify identity with valid government-issued photo documents, corroborate source of wealth and source of funds, and reject any shell-company indicators. Politically exposed persons require senior management approval, independent UBO confirmation, transaction monitoring, and quarterly re-screening.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Online Registry Portal (Internet Registration Office / Commercial Name Clearance and Registration System)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name in the Korean commercial register must be written in Hangul. A foreign family office may use a Hangul transliteration of its common English name; the English trade name may be added in parallel only after the Hangul name is approved. The four-tier naming convention requires (1) a distinct core identifier, (2) a permissible industry description, (3) the corporate form suffix Chusik Hoesa or Co., Ltd., and (4) a unique registry seat suffix; a name that is identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name is rejected by the registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: After rejection the applicant may file an objection within 14 days to the head of the District

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Korean Commercial Act (Korea Sangbeop), Act No. 1000, promulgated December 20, 1962, as amended most recently by Act No. 19111 (January 2, 2023); in particular Articles 288 through 371 (formation and governance of a stock corporation / chusik hoesa), Article 289 (matters to be stated in the Articles of Incorporation), Article 295 (incorporators' subscription), Article 301 (deposit of subscription price), Article 305 (the Inaugural General Meeting), Article 317 (registration of incorporation within three weeks of the inaugural meeting), and Articles 386 through 408 (representative director and statutory officers). For non-resident investors the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 19036, 2022), Articles 2 and 5, and the Enforcement Decree provisions on foreign direct investment notification also apply.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Office (Commercial Registration Division of the Local District Court; in Korean, beop-won deung-gi-gwa / sang-eop-deung-gi-so) having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, administered by the Courts Administration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea; electronic filing is accepted through the Internet Registration System (IROS / inteonet-deung-gi-so).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation (jusik-hoesa-seollib-deunggi-sincheongseo) filed under Article 317 of the Korean Commercial Act, accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation (jeong-gwan), the Inaugural General Meeting minutes, the Capital Subscription Deposit Certificate, and the written consents to registration of the statutory officers.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None as a strict statutory minimum: the former minimum paid-up capital of KRW 50,000,000 for stock corporations was abolished by Act No. 10267, effective April 15, 2012, and the Korean Commercial Act now imposes no minimum capital floor. Nevertheless, at least one share must be validly issued and the entire subscription price must be deposited, prior to the Inaugural General Meeting, into an escrow-type capital deposit account maintained with a domestic commercial bank or licensed securities brokerage in Korea; the depository must issue a Capital Subscription Deposit Certificate (jabon-geum-nap-ip-bogwan-jeungmyeongseo) evidencing the deposit, and the deposited funds are blocked from withdrawal until the incorporation registration has been completed by the court. For a single-family office the recommended operational substance is approximately KRW 100,000,000 (about USD 74,000) so as to support bank onboarding, enhanced due diligence, and the private banking and securities custody arrangements contemplated by the target payment rails.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 2025-001 OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [FAMILY HOLDINGS CO., LTD.], A CHUSIK HOESA, ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF AN ACTUAL MEETING, DATED [________], 2025. WHEREAS, the Company is a stock corporation (chusik hoesa) formed, or in the course of being formed, under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), with its registered office to be established at [Registered Office Address], Republic of Korea; WHEREAS, the incorporators have notarized and adopted the Articles of Incorporation, subscribed for all of the authorized shares of the Company, and deposited the entire subscription price in escrow with [Depository Bank], as evidenced by the Capital Subscription Deposit Certificate, all in accordance with Articles 289, 295, and 301 of the Commercial Act; WHEREAS, the undersigned individuals constitute the Board of Directors duly elected at the Inaugural General Meeting of Shareholders and now lawfully succeed to the statutory powers of the incorporators under Article 393 of the Commercial Act; WHEREAS, the Board has determined that the adoption of a registered office, the ratification of share capital, the designation of banking and custody institutions, and the appointment of statutory officers are necessary and prudent for the lawful commencement of the Company's single-family-office private investment holding business. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED as follows: 1. SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION RATIFICATION. The Board ratifies, confirms, and accepts the subscription and issuance of [____] ordinary shares, par value KRW [____] each, representing total paid-in capital of KRW [____], to the founding shareholders named in the share register, and directs the Representative Director to maintain the shareholder register and capital records in accordance with Articles 302, 306, 317, and 353 of the Commercial Act in a manner open to statutory inspection. 2. BANKING, CUSTODY, AND PAYMENT AUTHORIZATION. The Board designates [Bank A] and [Bank B] as the principal depositories, custodians, and payment banks of the Company for private-banking wire transfers and securities custody. The Representative Director, acting alone for transactions not exceeding KRW [Threshold] and otherwise jointly with any other director, is hereby authorized to open, maintain, pledge, and close any current, deposit, custody, or brokerage account, to execute signature cards, account agreements, custody agreements, and payment instructions, and to direct the investment of family-office assets consistently with the approved investment policy. Each designated bank is authorized to rely on this resolution until written revocation reaches the bank. 3. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the Company is hereby fixed and adopted at [Full Address], Republic of Korea, being the statutory seat for venue, notice, service of process, tax domicile, and registry jurisdiction. The Representative Director is authorized to execute the lease or sublease, to register the office with the competent Commercial Registration Office, and to post any required public notice. 4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The Board appoints [Name A] as Representative Director (Dae-Pyo I-Sa), [Name B] as Internal Director, and [Name C] as statutory Auditor (Gam-Sa), each to serve until the next annual general meeting and until a successor is duly qualified. The Auditor shall perform independent oversight of the Company's accounting and financial records pursuant to Articles 409 through 412 of the Commercial Act and shall report any irregularities to the shareholders. 5. CORPORATE SEAL AND EXECUTION. The corporate seal (beobin-in-gam) of the Company, an impression of which is affixed in the minute book, is adopted and shall be registered with the court registry and the tax office. Any instrument executed by the Representative Director under the corporate seal shall be conclusively binding on the Company. 6. IMPLEMENTATION AND DELEGATION. The Representative Director is authorized and directed to make, execute, deliver, notarize, and register all applications, consents to registration, tax filings, bank forms, and any other documents required to perfect the establishment of the Company and to consummate the foregoing resolutions, and to take every further step which he or she, in professional judgment, deems necessary or advisable. RESOLVED FURTHER, that all acts performed by the incorporators or directors prior to this resolution that are within the scope of the foregoing are hereby ratified, confirmed, and adopted as acts of the Company. This resolution shall be effective as of the date first written above and shall continue in full force and effect until revoked or superseded by a subsequent resolution of the Board. ADOPTED by the unanimous written consent of the entire Board of Directors this [Date]. [Signature Block of Directors].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search, Articles of Incorporation Drafting, and Notarization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internet Registration Office (IROS) of the Supreme Court of Korea for name reservation (inteonet-deung-gi-so), and a Notary Public of the Korea Notary Association for attestation of the Articles of Incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name availability search on the IROS portal (www.iros.go.kr) to confirm that the proposed Korean-language trade name and the parallel English name of the family office holding company are not identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered entity; reserve the approved name for the statutory reservation period. Draft the Articles of Incorporation (jeong-gwan) in the Korean language in strict compliance with Article 289 of the Commercial Act, setting forth the corporate purpose in a deliberately narrow formulation limited to private investment holding and single-family-office administration, the precise number of authorized shares with par value, the aggregate stated capital, the planned registered office address, the term of the company if limited, the method of public notice, and the board composition including provision for a statutory auditor. Submit the draft articles to a licensed Korean notary public for formal attestation; the notarization step is mandatory because the registry will not accept unregistered articles. Ensure that the notarized articles, and all subsequent official documents, consistently match the English trade name '[Family Holdings] Co., Ltd.' used in the KR entity formation payload.
required_dossiers: Proposed Korean and English corporate trade names for IROS search and reservation
Draft Articles of Incorporation (jeong-gwan) in Korean
Certificate of personal seal (in-gam-jeung-myeong) or passport copy of each incorporator
Notarization appointment form and identity documents of all incorporators
Power of attorney if any incorporator is represented by an agent, with notarized signature
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is refused on grounds of confusing similarity, immediately submit an alternative name candidate list and re-reserve through IROS; if the notary public questions the purpose clauses as too broad for an unlicensed investment vehicle, amend the articles to narrow the corporate purpose to Articles 6430 trust and investment holding activities and resubmit the amended text for notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share Subscription and Escrow Deposit of Paid-in Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Domestic commercial bank or licensed securities brokerage in the Republic of Korea acting as the capital deposit escrow institution under Article 301 of the Commercial Act; Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or an authorized foreign exchange bank for any required Foreign Direct Investment notification.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a formal share subscription certificate (jusik-cheong-yakseo) for each incorporator, by which each incorporator subscribes to at least one ordinary share at a non-zero par value. Open a company formation escrow deposit account (hoesa-seollib-napib-yecho-gae-jwa) with the chosen domestic banking institution and remit the full amount of the subscription price, representing 100 percent of the stated paid-in capital, into that blocked account before the convocation of the Inaugural General Meeting. Obtain the Capital Subscription Deposit Certificate (jabon-geum-nap-ip-bogwan-jeungmyeongseo) from the depository, stating the deposit date, the total amount, the depositor identity, and the account number; this certificate is an indispensable attachment to the incorporation registration filing. Where any shareholder is a non-resident individual or entity, complete the foreign direct investment notification procedure with KOTRA or the relevant foreign exchange bank if the investment amount reaches the statutory threshold, and retain the notification receipt for bank onboarding and registry inspection. The deposited capital remains frozen until the court completes the incorporation registration; no withdrawals may be made in the interim.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Share subscription certificates (jusik-cheong-yakseo) executed by each incorporator
Incorporators' identification documents (Korean resident ID or passport)
Power of attorney and notarized signature of the principal, if subscribed by an agent
Incorporation escrow account application forms of the domestic depository bank
Capital Subscription Deposit Certificate (jabon-geum-nap-ip-bogwan-jeungmyeongseo)
Foreign direct investment notification receipt from KOTRA or the foreign exchange bank, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the escrow account application or issues a deficient deposit certificate, request reissuance with corrected particulars; if the bank raises AML or source-of-wealth queries owing to the family-office profile, submit a source-of-funds declaration, prior tax clearance, and a family wealth structure statement, and if still refused, apply to an alternative licensed depository institution and secure an unqualified deposit certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convocation of the Inaugural General Meeting and Election of Directors and Auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inaugural General Meeting of Incorporators (bal-gi-in-chong-hoe) convened by the incorporators; minutes must be prepared in writing and, where prudent or when specifically demanded by the registry, notarized or certified by the notary public.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the Inaugural General Meeting only after the full subscription price has been deposited and the Capital Subscription Deposit Certificate has been issued. At the meeting, the incorporators shall adopt or finally ratify the notarized Articles, receive and approve the statutory establishment report (seollib-sahang-bogo) describing the incorporation procedures, elect the directors and the statutory auditor by a majority of the voting rights present, and pass a resolution authorizing the appointment of the Representative Director (Dae-Pyo I-Sa). Prepare and execute formal minutes (ui-sa-rok) signed by the chairperson and the attending incorporators, and obtain from each newly elected director and auditor a written letter of acceptance (seung-nak-seo), a personal seal certificate (in-gam-jeung-myeong) or notarized signature specimen, and a written consent to registration (deung-gi-eung-nak-seo) authorizing the filing of their appointments with the court. For a single-family-office holding company with paid-in capital above the statutory thresholds, or where the company is deemed a large enterprise, an independent auditor is required; otherwise, a non-statutory auditor may lawfully serve. Verify the quorum and voting calculations against the subscribed share list before adjournment.
required_dossiers: Notice or written waiver of notice for the Inaugural General Meeting
Establishment report (seollib-sahang-bogo) prepared by the incorporators
Minutes of the Inaugural General Meeting (ui-sa-rok) signed by the chairperson
Written acceptance (seung-nak-seo) of each elected director and auditor
Personal seal certificate (in-gam-jeung-myeong) or notarized signature specimen of each officer
Written consent to registration (deung-gi-eung-nak-seo) of each officer
Share subscription allocation list identifying all shareholders and their shareholdings
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court later issues a supplemental order (bo-wan-myeng-ryeong) objecting to the form or content of the minutes, reconvene or execute a supplementary written resolution curing the identified defect and refile the corrected minutes; if a director or auditor election is challenged, hold a supplementary general meeting, re-vote on the officer slate, and file the revised resolutions before the registration deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Registration with the Commercial Registration Office of the District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office (Sang-eop Deung-gi-so) of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; electronic submission through the Supreme Court IROS e-registration portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within three weeks from the closing of the Inaugural General Meeting, as mandated by Article 317(1) of the Commercial Act, file the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation (jusik-hoesa-seollib-deung-gi-sin-cheong-seo) with the competent District Court Commercial Registration Office. Attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the Inaugural General Meeting minutes, the Capital Subscription Deposit Certificate, the consent to registration and seal certificates of each director and the auditor, the list of incorporators, and any required power-of-attorney documents for the filing agent. Compute and pay the court registration fee, which is calculated as 0.04 percent of stated capital with a statutory minimum floor of KRW 40,000, plus a 20 percent local education surtax, totaling approximately KRW 48,000 (about USD 36) for a standard single-family-office capitalization. After the court examines the filing and accepts the registration, obtain the official Certificate of Registered Matters (deung-gi-sa-hang-jeung-myeong-seo) and simultaneously complete the corporate seal registration (beobin-in-gam-sin-go) at the same registry. The company acquires legal personality and is deemed incorporated as of the moment of registration.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation (jusik-hoesa-seollib-deung-gi-sin-cheong-seo)
Notarized Articles of Incorporation (jeong-gwan)
Minutes of the Inaugural General Meeting (ui-sa-rok)
Capital Subscription Deposit Certificate (jabon-geum-nap-ip-bogwan-jeungmyeongseo)
Written consents to registration (deung-gi-eung-nak-seo) with seal certificates of all directors and the auditor
Identity documents and seal certificates of the incorporators
Power of attorney of the filing agent, if any, with corporate seal
Receipt of payment of the registration fee and education surtax
Pro-forma corporation ledger sheet prescribed by the court
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a supplemental order or suspension notice citing incomplete documentation, cure each defect within the statutory grace period (ordinarily two weeks) by refiling corrected and notarized documents; if registration is refused outright, rectify the disqualifying circumstance, such as an invalid capital deposit certificate or unauthorized officer appointment, and re-file a fresh application with a recalculated fee; a refusal may be challenged through the registry's objection procedure governed by the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, AML, Bank, and Employment Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) local tax office (se-mu-seo) via the HomeTax (hom-taek-seu) portal; the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) of the Financial Services Commission for AML reporting-entity registration if applicable; the local municipal government for local taxes; and the four social insurance agencies (National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service, and Employment Insurance system) if staff are engaged.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days from the date of incorporation registration, file the Business Registration Application (sa-eop-ja-deung-rok-sin-cheong-seo) with the competent NTS local tax office through HomeTax, stating the corporate purpose, registered office, and representative director, and receive the Business Registration Certificate (sa-eop-ja-deung-rok-jeung). Register the corporate seal impression for tax certificate issuance and obtain the corporate seal certificate (beobin-in-gam-jeung-myeong-seo). Open operating and private-banking accounts at the target depositories, completing full AML/KYC procedures that include identification of the beneficial owners of the family office, submission of the source-of-wealth declaration, and, given the medium-risk enhanced tier, cooperation with the bank's enhanced due diligence measures under the Act on Reporting and Using of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Teukjeong-Geumyung-Jeongbo-Beop); if the family office acts as a reporting entity by conducting any designated financial transactions, register accordingly with KoFIU. File the local tax registrations with the municipal government for annual property tax and local income tax purposes. If the office intends to hire administrative staff, complete the four mandatory social insurance registrations within fourteen days, issue written employment contracts, and comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act workplace requirements before operations commence.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registered Matters (deung-gi-sa-hang-jeung-myeong-seo) from the court
Corporate seal certificate (beobin-in-gam-jeung-myeong-seo) and seal registration transcript
Business Registration Application (sa-eop-ja-deung-rok-sin-cheong-seo)
Notarized Articles of Incorporation and lease agreement for the registered office
Foreign direct investment notification receipt, if applicable
Beneficial owner identification form and source-of-wealth declaration for AML/KYC
Passport or Korean ID copies of the representative director and other officers
Bank account application forms and signature cards for the private banking and custody accounts
Employment records and social insurance enrollment applications, only if hiring personnel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS queries or delays the business registration due to the passive holding purpose, submit the incorporation registration transcript together with a family-office charter and investment policy letter confirming the absence of commercial trading activities; if a bank declines account opening under enhanced due diligence, file a written source-of-wealth and family-structure disclosure, escalate to the bank compliance officer, or transfer the relationship to an alternative licensed institution; if the social insurance agencies reject enrollment for missing employment records, recompute payroll and re-file with corrected contracts within the statutory cure period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the entity is a pure private investment holding vehicle and single-family office (ISIC 6430 / NAICS 525920) with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations, and therefore no industrial licensing board or municipal agency operating-license clearance is mandatory. If the family office should in the future establish physical facilities, the competent authorities would be the relevant municipal government (Si/Gun/Gu industrial licensing windows) and, where applicable, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) licensing bureaus.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - the vehicle does not require a statutory operating or manufacturing permit and is license-free for its passive holding activity; any future third-party discretionary asset management or financial investment business would require licensing by the Financial Services Commission (FSC) under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (ME) of the Republic of Korea; Not Applicable to this scope
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), Prior Environmental Review System (PERS), or Environmental Registration is required under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act (EIAA) because the formation of a holding company creates no physical development footprint, industrial facility, or emission source.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the entity generates zero wastewater, volatile organic compounds (VOC), or hazardous waste. For forward-compliance reference, if the company later adds office or warehouse facilities, the applicable quantitative thresholds would include the Water Environment Conservation Act permissible effluent limits (BOD, COD, SS, and total phosphorus concentrations dependent on discharge volume and watercourse classification), the Clean Air Conservation Act VOC control requirements for solvent-using equipment (typically a processing-loss capture ratio standard applicable above stated annual solvent throughput), and the Wastes Control Act hazardous-waste manifesting with a thirty-day on-site storage limit, all enforced by the regional environmental agency superintended by the Ministry of Environment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for industrial civil-defense fire permits, structural load inspections, or workplace safety certification because the company will operate only as a leasehold administrative office for a family-office investment holding business. Nevertheless, the company must procure from the building owner evidence of the fire-safety installation completion inspection certificate (so-bang-si-seol-wan-bi-geom-sa-pil-jeung) under the Fire Facility Installation Maintenance and Safety Management Act, comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act for office workplaces including the basic annual safety and health inspection applicable to businesses with fewer than fifty employees, and participate in mandatory civil-defense emergency evacuation drills prescribed by the Framework Act on the Management of Disasters and Safety; if a warehouse is ever added, a separate Civil Defense fire permit and structural load inspection by the local fire department would become mandatory.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea via the HomeTax electronic portal at https://www.hometax.go.kr; export customs clearance and export declarations are administered separately by the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS portal at https://unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity intending to carry on a taxable business in the Republic of Korea must first appoint a legal tax representative if it has no domestic place of business. The entity or its tax representative must file an Application for Business Registration with the relevant district tax office of the National Tax Service, either in writing or through HomeTax, accompanied by the entity's constitutional documents, evidence of foreign registration, certification of the representative director and address, and proof of the domestic place of business or tax representative appointment. Upon approval, the NTS issues the Business Registration Number, a ten-digit identifier that functions simultaneously as the VAT identification number and the general national tax identification number for corporate tax, VAT, customs declarations, e-invoice exchange and foreign investment reporting. No separate TIN or VAT ID is issued to a non-resident entity without a Korean taxable establishment, but such an entity must still obtain a Business Registration Number if it makes supplies subject to Korean VAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not operate a check-the-box or elective entity classification regime for domestic corporations. A Chusik Hoesa is uniformly taxable as a resident corporation at the entity level under the Corporate Tax Act. Hybrid mismatch rules are statutorily applied, but no elective hybrid mismatch classification is available to a Korean-resident company.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold is prescribed for VAT registration: any person or entity supplying taxable goods or services in the Republic of Korea is required to register from the date of business commencement, irrespective of annual turnover. A separate simplified taxable person regime applies only to eligible natural persons whose annual taxable revenue is below the statutory threshold currently prescribed by Presidential Decree (approximately KRW 80,000,000, subject to legislative indexation); this does not exempt them from the obligation to obtain a Business Registration Number but only affects reporting and liability computation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices are mandatory for all corporations, including a Chusik Hoesa. Invoices must be issued through the HomeTax electronic tax invoice system or through an NTS-approved electronic tax invoice service provider using machine-readable XML/API interfaces; the invoice data is transmitted to the NTS at the time of issuance or within the statutory reporting period, and the NTS assigns a unique tax invoice number for matching in VAT returns. The Republic of Korea does not currently operate a transactional fiscal stamping device or a pre-clearance model requiring government approval before invoice issuance; integrity is maintained through NTS-controlled invoice numbering, cross-matching against VAT filings, and penalty surcharges for non-issued, erroneous, or late-transmitted electronic tax invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A zero rate applies where legal ownership of goods is transferred to a foreign purchaser and the goods are physically exported from Korea under the customs export procedure, as evidenced by an accepted export declaration. Zero-rating also applies to qualifying services performed outside Korea, services supplied to non-resident recipients and paid in foreign currency in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, international transportation services, and services directly connected with exported goods. The supplier must be able to evidence the actual export from Korea and the receipt of sales proceeds in convertible foreign currency within the statutory repatriation window.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Bill of Entry / Declaration of Export Goods) filed with and returned by the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS electronic clearance system
Bill of Lading (sea), Air Waybill (air), or multimodal transport document evidencing physical exportation from Korea

Inward Foreign Exchange Payment Confirmation / Foreign Exchange Transaction Certificate (equivalent to a Foreign Exchange Remittance Certificate, FIRC) issued by a Korean Foreign Exchange Bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
Commercial invoice, packing list, export sales contract, and any invoice-level ledger reconciling the Korean supplier, foreign buyer, zero-rated supply value, and foreign currency remittance
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service and the Korea Customs Service jointly audit export zero-rating claims by matching export declarations, electronic tax invoices, foreign exchange transaction records, and cargo movements. Where the required customs documentation or foreign exchange repatriation evidence is incomplete or false, the NTS reverses the zero-rating and assesses VAT at 10% on the supply value, together with statutory interest. Additional penalties are imposable under the Framework Act on National Taxes, including negligent underreporting penalties, intentional underreporting and fraud penalties up to 40% of the evaded tax, invoice-related penalties of 1% of the supply value per missing or false electronic tax invoice, and criminal sanctions under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act in cases of fraudulent substitution or fabricated export documentation. The ordinary reassessment limitation period is five years, extended to ten years for fraudulent concealment, allowing retrospective clawback of unsubstantiated zero-rated export claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with policy and enforcement cooperation from the Ministry of Economy and Finance through designated foreign exchange banks
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalized but closely supervised foreign exchange regime. The Korean won is fully convertible for bona fide current account transactions, including trade-related payments, service fees, dividends, and profit remittances, subject to standard bank verification and supporting documentation. Exporters are not required to surrender hard currency; however, export proceeds must be collected within the statutory collection period, normally six months from the date of export declaration, and any delay must be justified and extended via the reporting foreign exchange bank or BOK. Capital account transactions are more restricted: foreign direct investment, overseas borrowing, external lending, and portfolio investments require notification, registration, or approval depending on size and counterparty. For a Korean Chusik Hoesa structured as a single family office, inbound equity injections and subsequent outbound distributions or loan repayments must be booked through a designated foreign exchange bank using the correct transaction codes and supporting corporate documents. The Government has gradually deregulated since the 1997 and 2008 crises, but macro-prudential limits on currency mismatches, short-term external borrowing, and derivative positions remain. Profit remittance hurdles are low if audited financial statements, tax compliance certificates, and board resolutions are presented; dividends and liquidation proceeds are generally freely remittable after withholding tax obligations. Overall, the won is convertible for ordinary trade and investment flows, but every capital transaction must be traceable, documented, and aligned with BOK reporting thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory percentage conversion or surrender requirement for Korean export proceeds; exporters may retain foreign currency proceeds in designated foreign exchange accounts. However, the export receipts must be collected within 6 months from the export declaration date under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and related regulations. If collection is delayed beyond 6 months, the exporter must file a delay report with the relevant foreign exchange bank and obtain an extension, typically limited to another 6 months unless exceptional circumstances are proven.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Currency Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational KRW Account
Foreign Currency Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational KRW Account
Foreign Currency Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational KRW Account
Foreign Currency Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational KRW Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) have very limited viability in South Korea for corporate treasury operations. Korean law does not recognize a standalone EMI charter equivalent to European e-money institutions; entities are classified as electronic financial businesses under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and are restricted to payment services, not deposit-taking or corporate equity capital escrow. They cannot issue accounts that support capital verification, foreign investor registration, FX conversion, or trade settlement in a legally compliant manner. Consequently, fintech EMIs are not a viable alternative for the Chusik Hoesa single family office; all regulated cross-border liquidity clearing must route through licensed domestic banks with foreign exchange dealing authority.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly formed foreign-invested Chusik Hoesa, the statutory directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) must appear in person at a licensed Korean bank branch or, where in-person attendance is impossible, must provide a notarized and apostilled power of attorney coupled with live video verification by the bank's compliance officer. Remote-only account opening for a non-resident-owned private investment holding entity is generally not permitted under the Specific Financial Information Act and BOK supervision guidance. The bank will require an in-branch or financial-station meeting for at least one authorized signatory who holds the economic substance of the account, and the UBO's identity must be verified against original passports, visa documents, and alien registration certificates where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth and original funds for high-net-worth family assets cannot be adequately explained by the stated income of the contributing family member
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A comprehensive 24-month source of wealth report including audited financial statements of the direct wealth-generating operating companies, certified personal and corporate income tax returns, bank and brokerage statements from the originating jurisdiction, title deeds or sale and purchase agreements for disposed assets, and a notarized letter of explanation reconciling the entire capital contribution to documented accumulated income.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain opacity through multi-layered family trusts, foundations, or intermediary holding vehicles
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A full corporate/ownership waterfall chart showing all intermediate entities, official UBO registry extracts or equivalent certifications from the relevant jurisdictions, certified copies of trust deeds and trustee appointments, passports of all natural persons above the defined control threshold, and a legal opinion from a licensed counsel confirming the ultimate beneficial owners and absence of undisclosed principals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential regulatory interpretation of a single family office as an unlicensed asset management or collective investment business
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A Korean legal opinion confirming that the Chusik Hoesa will engage solely in passive investment in the assets of a single family, the company's articles of incorporation explicitly restricting third-party money management, a board resolution adopting a passive investment policy, audited or management accounts evidencing no external client funds, and a written declaration that no inducement or solicitation of outside capital will be made.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment flow mismatches or high-risk counterparty exposure, such as receivables from sanctioned jurisdictions or unexplained crypto-asset proceeds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty due diligence files with valid sanctions and adverse-media screening results, original commercial contracts or investment agreements showing the economic rationale for each wire, detailed payment flow charts tracing each transfer from origin to destination, bank statements in the source country, and if any crypto exposure exists, a full transaction report including wallet addresses, exchange records, and source-of-funds attestation from qualified exchange platforms.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections into the Chusik Hoesa must be structured as foreign direct investment equity contributions. The foreign investor must file a foreign investment notification with a designated foreign exchange bank or the Invest KOREA center before remitting funds, obtain a foreign investment registration certificate, open a domestic foreign currency account and a KRW corporate operating account, and wire the funds via SWIFT MT103 using the purpose code for equity investment or capital contribution. Upon receipt, the bank verifies the source of funds, converts foreign currency to KRW through the domestic foreign exchange market at the market or agreed rate, and issues a capital verification certificate confirming the paid-in capital. The transaction must be recorded with BOK/foreign exchange bank reporting; a post-investment report must be filed within 30 days of capital settlement, and the company's commercial registry must reflect the capital increase before any withdrawal is permitted.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and operational disbursements are cleared through standard banking rails: SWIFT MT103 direct payments for supplier invoices, service fees, dividends, royalties, and intercompany payments; Commercial Letters of Credit (L/Cs) for purchase contracts of goods requiring documentary security; and Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) for lower-risk open-account deliveries or sample transactions. All outbound payments must be accompanied by underlying contracts, invoices, customs declarations, and tax clearance documents, and must use approved Korean purpose-of-payment codes. Dividend remittances require board approval, audited financial statements, tax payment confirmations, and a remittance resolution. Foreign exchange banks will screen every transaction against the Bank of Korea, FATF, US OFAC, EU, and other applicable sanctions lists before execution.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts with a documented real economic exposure, such as future export receipts, import payables, or equity repatriation obligations
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts for KRW hedging executed through onshore banks or offshore counterparties in accordance with BOK macro-prudential limits

Plain vanilla Korean won currency options and exchange-traded (or OTC) swaps used solely for hedging the family office's balance-sheet currency risk, with no speculative or naked derivative positioning

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary general shareholders' meeting and approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal governance record kept in the corporate minute book at the registered office; registrable resolutions filed with the Commercial Registration Office of the competent District Court
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months from the close of each business year; for a calendar year-end Chusik Hoesa, on or before March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No annual government filing fee; failure to convene punctually exposes directors to shareholder derivative claims, court-ordered convocation, and legal inability to approve dividend distributions or discharge directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report and audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission / Financial Supervisory Service through the DART electronic system; Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants for auditor registration matters; copy attached to the National Tax Service filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a company subject to statutory external audit, no later than the date of the annual shareholders' meeting and in any event within three months after the fiscal year-end; extension of the meeting deadline does not extend the audit report delivery beyond the statutory audit workflow
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain or file an audit report triggers corrective orders, administrative fines of up to KRW 20 million (approximately USD 15,000), forced appointment of an auditor at the company's expense, and rejection of the financial statements as valid corporate records for dividend or tax purposes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and annual financial statement schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service through Hometax / competent District Tax Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of the third month following the fiscal year-end; March 31 for a calendar-year company; a one-month extension may be available with a valid explanation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax; under-reporting penalty of 10% of the omitted tax; late-payment surcharge of 0.022% per day; tax seizure and collection procedures; if the company is dormant for one year or more, the tax authority may ex officio close the business registration and the court may strike off the entity after the dormancy procedure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate local income tax surcharge return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service, collected together with the national corporate tax return and then allocated to the local government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the corporate income tax deadline; March 31 for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfaithful-return and non-payment penalties are applied on the local income tax in addition to the national corporate tax penalties, including the 0.022% daily late-payment surcharge.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax and tax invoice compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Semi-annual VAT filing windows: January 25 for the second half of the prior year and July 25 for the first half of the year; tax invoices for taxable supplies must generally be issued by the 10th day of the following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unreported VAT penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax; late-payment surcharge of 0.022% per day; failure to issue or correct tax invoices may additionally attract penalty taxes under the Value-Added Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Payroll withholding returns, annual employment income reconciliation, and four major social insurance filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service; National Pension Service; National Health Insurance Service; Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service; employment and industrial accident insurance collection agencies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly withholding and social insurance contributions by the 10th of the following month; annual employment income reconciliation and tax statements due in February generally; no filing obligation if the single-family office has no employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Withholding tax omission penalties and 0.022% daily late-payment surcharges; social insurance delinquencies can produce collection orders and administrative fines; responsible directors may be personally assessed for unpaid withheld taxes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial registration record update for directors, auditors, registered officers, capital, or registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the competent District Court
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two weeks after the event requiring registration; there is no annual commercial registration renewal obligation in Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No automatic annual penalty, but unregistered matters cannot be asserted against bona fide third parties; continued failure to maintain valid registration after the company becomes dormant may lead to court dissolution and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholder register maintenance and annual shareholder list attachment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate register at the registered office; annual shareholder list is filed as an attachment to the corporate income tax return with the National Tax Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder register must be continuously current; the annual shareholder list is due with the corporate income tax return by March 31 for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or omitted shareholder list can trigger unfaithful-return penalties and evidentiary disadvantages in tax audits; failure to record a transferee in the register prevents the transferee from exercising shareholder rights against the company.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 2 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Chusik Hoesa must undergo an independent certified public accountant audit when (i) total assets at the end of the preceding business year equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9,200,000); (ii) the company is a listed issuer, financial company, or entity designated by the Financial Services Commission; (iii) the company is an asset-backed securitization special purpose company or a public-interest entity designated by Presidential Decree; or (iv) the company is part of a consolidated group whose consolidated total assets exceed the same KRW 12 billion balance-sheet threshold. The legal test is primarily balance-sheet based; ordinary private holding companies are not subject to a separate turnover or headcount trigger, although the Financial Services Commission may designate additional companies based on public interest criteria. A single-family office holding substantial family investment assets will almost always cross the KRW 12 billion threshold and therefore require a statutory CPA audit and Korean certified auditor engagement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) are mandatory for listed companies and certain public-interest entities; non-listed Chusik Hoesa may prepare financial statements under Korean GAAP, including the Korean Accounting Standards for Small and Medium Enterprises, when not required to adopt K-IFRS. Audits must be performed under Korean Standards on Auditing issued by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants, aligned with international auditing standards. Records supporting the audit and annual tax filings must be retained at least 7 years; Korean Commercial Act separately requires commercial books and settlement documents to be retained for 10 years.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No central annual UBO declaration is filed in South Korea for a private Chusik Hoesa. The statutory obligation is to maintain a complete register of shareholders at the registered office; a share transfer is enforceable against the company only when the transferee is recorded in that register, and the company must update the register without undue delay after receiving valid notice and supporting documentation. For annual tax compliance, the company must attach a complete shareholder list showing holders, share counts, acquisition dates, and tax residence to the corporate income tax return. For foreign investors acquiring Korean shares, the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act imposes a 30-day reporting window through a designated foreign exchange bank or securities custodian. Material share ownership or control changes that also alter directors or registered officers must be recorded in the commercial registration file with the District Court within two weeks. Financial institutions performing AML customer due diligence may also require current beneficial ownership identification; falsifying the shareholder register or UBO records may result in administrative fines and criminal liability.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% national corporate income tax on taxable income exceeding KRW 30 billion; 22% for KRW 20 billion to 30 billion; 20% for KRW 200 million to 20 billion; 10% for first KRW 200 million; plus 10% local income tax surcharge (effective top rate 27.5%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Tax credits for R&D (up to 30-40% of qualifying expenses under TIPA and National Tax Act), foreign-investment incentives under FFEIA, Free Economic Zone tax reductions, job creation credits; no specific patent box for family offices, but capital gains from listed securities may be tax-exempt for non-dealers

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return Form 1 for Domestic Corporations filed electronically via HomeTax (National Tax Service e-filing system), with attached financial statements (K-GAAP or IFRS) and tax reconciliation schedules
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; mid-year preliminary tax payments (interim prepayments) are due by August 31 for fiscal years ending December 31
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing and payment due within 3 months after the fiscal year-end (March 31 for December year-end); extensions available with tax representation for up to 1 month without penalty if properly filed

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business income (total revenue from all sources, including interest, dividends, and capital gains)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all worldwide income as a Korean tax resident company. For a single-family office, include both Korean-sourced and foreign income; foreign taxes will be credited at Box 5.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses (cost of sales, operating expenses, depreciation, amortization, and other ordinary tax-deductible costs)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only statutory deductible expenditures. Related-party payments must satisfy arm's length standard; non-deductible foreign taxes, fines, excess interest (thin-capitalization), and non-statutory reserves must be adjusted out.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before special deductions (tax base after book-to-tax adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply special reserves and tax-exemption provisions carefully. For an SFO, capital gains from listed securities may be tax-exempt unless the company trades as a substantial shareholder or security dealer; cross-border dividends from 10%+ foreign subsidiaries may qualify for indirect credit under CFC rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate tax computed at progressive statutory rates on taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute using marginal rates 10% up to KRW 200M, 20% up to KRW 20B, 22% up to KRW 30B, and 25% above KRW 30B. No special rate applies merely because shareholders are non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (foreign tax credit, R&D credits, temporary investment tax credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credit is limited to Korean corporate tax attributable to foreign-source income; unilateral credit is available under domestic law even without a treaty. Evidence of foreign tax paid must be retained and translated if necessary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local income tax surcharge (qualification surtax) at 10% of the national corporate tax payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report and pay the local income tax surcharge together with the national tax; no separate local return is required for corporations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable (or refund) to be remitted to the National Tax Service
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All payments must be made to designated tax collection accounts. Any prior overpayment is automatically offset; refunds may be applied for in the same return. If non-resident shareholders expect dividends, ensure that reduced DTA withholding is separately claimed on the shareholder level.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: underpaid tax penalty of 0.022% per day (maximum 36 months) plus 20% negligence tax on unpaid tax; fraudulent return triggers 40% penalty. Failing to submit attached documents: up to KRW 500,000 per document. Criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for willful omission; directors may be jointly liable for unpaid tax caused by gross negligence or fraud.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national withholding tax on dividends plus 2% local income tax surcharge) under Korean domestic law, unless reduced by a Double Tax Agreement; typical DTA rates range from 5% to 15% depending on ownership and treaty
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced DTA withholding, the distributing company must obtain from the shareholder a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), a residence and beneficial ownership declaration (Form 24/25 for reduced-rate withholding), and evidence of the right to treaty benefits. Submit these documents to the withholding agent before payment or apply for a refund within 5 years after the calendar year of withholding. The OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test may deny treaty benefits if the shareholder is a conduit lacking substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic statutory 22% gross (20% national + 2% local); typical treaty rate 10-15% (e.g., US/UK). Interest: domestic statutory 22%; treaty rates generally 10% for bank loans and 15% for other interest. Intercompany interest must also comply with thin-capitalization rules (debt-to-equity ratio 3:1; excess interest is non-deductible).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 500 million for annual tangible-asset transactions, KRW 50 million for intangible-property or royalty transactions, and KRW 50 million for services, per foreign related party per year; local file mandatory above these thresholds. Master file required if consolidated revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not have a BVI-style Economic Substance Regulation. However, substance-over-form, place-of-effective-management, and CFC rules apply. A Chusik Hoesa acting as a single-family office must maintain real business presence and perform core income-generating activities (CIGA) in Korea to retain Korean tax residence and treaty access. A purely passive shell lacking employees, office, or meeting minutes may be disqualified under BEPS Action 5 and the Principal Purpose Test, triggering full Korean taxation and treaty denial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally reconstructing records, misstating revenue, fabricating expenses, or concealing foreign bank accounts in the corporate income tax return, causing underpayment of corporate tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Articles 10 and 11 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, up to 3 years' imprisonment or a fine not exceeding 3 times the evaded tax (aggravated to 5 years if evaded tax exceeds KRW 500 million). Additionally, a 40% negligence penalty under the Basic National Tax Collection Act and public disclosure on the tax-evader blacklist may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts may pierce the corporate veil when the company is a sham or the director abused limited liability. Directors can be jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax under the actual-business-operator doctrine; assets may be frozen and overseas travel banned. Criminal conviction leads to imprisonment, disqualification from board service, and civil restitution actions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance / Artificial Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into cross-border related-party transactions (management fees, royalties, interest, service fees) priced outside the arm's length range, or failing to prepare and submit transfer pricing documentation after exceeding the statutory thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Tax Adjustment Act Articles 4-8, the National Tax Service may adjust taxable income to the arm's length price, impose a 10% penalty on the underreported tax amount, and apply daily surcharges of up to 0.022%. Willful violations attract criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with fines and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign transfer pricing certification or knowingly approve inflated outbound payments may be treated as actual co-taxpayers; personal assets can be attached for the adjusted corporate tax. Travel bans, criminal indictment for aiding and abetting tax evasion, and breach-of-fiduciary-duty claims by family beneficiaries or minority shareholders are realistic consequences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Willful Failure to Withhold Non-Resident Taxes / Beneficial Ownership Misrepresentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, or royalties to non-resident shareholders or recipients without deducting statutory withholding tax, or claiming DTA relief through a shell conduit lacking economic substance, thereby misrepresenting beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding agents are liable for the unpaid tax plus additional charges of 10% (20% or 40% if intentional) under the Personal Income Tax Act and the Basic National Tax Collection Act. Article 12 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act imposes imprisonment of up to 2 years or a fine of up to 2 times the amount not withheld. Treaty benefits may be denied retroactively, with interest on all underpaid taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, as statutory withholding agents of the Chusik Hoesa, are personally liable for the unpaid withholding tax and penalties. Korean courts may issue overseas travel bans and enforce collection against director personal assets. Criminal conviction results in imprisonment, disqualification from corporate directorship, and severe reputational damage; in egregious cases, the corporate veil is pierced to hold directors personally accountable for the entire unpaid tax and criminal fines.
